end.summary:
Discussed how family members share household work and care for one another.
Trisha named cooking, school drop-off, medicine, sweeping, and mopping as family tasks.
Trisha repeatedly said children are too small to help and that only adults do family work.
Trisha later identified putting away books, bringing water, and taking out rubbish as possible tasks, but did not consistently count them as family work.
Trisha recognised that Papa can cook and that this can give Mummy rest; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Asha practised why sharing household work matters and that anyone in a family can help. Trisha named several care tasks and later noticed that Papa cooking can give Mummy a rest. There was a mix-up about children being too small to help and about personal tasks not counting as family work; this was not fully corrected by the end. At home, invite Trisha to choose one safe shared task, such as putting away books or bringing water, and talk about how it helps the family.
